column1: # Book 5 review (Fable, 2026-10-30). Finding 5.1409 accepted (genus is the subject). Secondaries 5.1386 (reperta passive) and 5.1408 (vigiles = the wakeful) accepted. 5.1362 rerum natura creatrix = "the nature of things herself, the creator", as at 1.629 and 2.1117; drafting note removed. 5.1385 taken verbatim from the Book 4 review text (4.585). 5.1393 verbatim with 2.30, 5.1394-1396 parallel to 2.31-33 in the past tense. 5.1388-1389 = 5.1454-1455 ("the shores of light", no dias; eruit = digs up, erigit = raises). 5.1373, 5.1387, 5.1404, 5.1415, 5.1439 brought into the band.

column2: was at first the nature of things herself, the creator,
so they might have them on hills and plains, and a strip of olives,
that the pipe pours out when struck by the players' fingers,
found out through pathless groves and woods and glades,
through the shepherds' lonely haunts and their leisure under the sky. {{NOTE: otia dia; dia may mean "divine" or "open-air"; Bailey takes it as leisure under the open sky}}

into the open, and reasoning digs it up to the shores of light. {{NOTE: refrain, repeated at 5.1454-1455 (eruit here, erigit there); luminis oras without dias, so not the full refrain "the shining shores of light"}}
beside a stream of water under the boughs of a tall tree,
with no great wealth they tended their bodies pleasantly,
above all when the weather smiled and the seasons
of the year painted the greening grass with flowers.
since all these things then flourished the more, new and wonderful.
from which even now the wakeful keep these customs handed down,
and the race has learned to keep the measure, and yet not a whit
destroys it and changes our feelings toward all things of old.
and that things go by a sure principle and in a sure order.
